title: EXTERNAL PROGRAM / ERROR NOTICE
lines: The command could not run. Check its DOS filename and PATH setting.
A missing program can also mean that its drive is not available.
Invalid executable format: verify that the file is a DOS program.
Insufficient memory: reduce other resident programs before retrying.
Enter or Escape returns from help to the error notice.
The next Enter or Escape dismisses the notice itself.
The notice timer pauses while help is open.
Left and Right select a topic. Up and Down scroll its text.
PageUp and PageDown move by a screen. Home and End move within a topic.
Press / to find text. Enter starts the search; Escape cancels it.
F3 continues after the matching line and wraps through the document.
CHECKING A COMMAND
Use a short DOS filename and confirm the file exists on the named drive.
A program may need support files in its current working directory.
Check that a batch command invokes the intended DOS program.
A damaged or incompatible executable can fail before it displays text.
Keep working files separate from the program's executable files.
Use the session, transfer and settings topics for related commands.

title: SERIAL SESSION / LOCAL INPUT
lines: Serial receive and flow control continue while help is displayed.
Incoming display bytes remain queued until the notice releases its view.
The bounded queue cannot store an unlimited incoming stream.
Help keys are local. They are not transmitted to the remote system.
The selected standard or enhanced BIOS keyboard mode remains in use.
Mouse direction events scroll or select topics. Enter returns.
The current session continues to control the serial modem connection.
Escape closes help. The next queued key still belongs to the notice.
Search finds command names and help text. ASCII letters ignore case.
A search can be canceled while the serial session remains active.
